c.tagline: Cobblestone history and college-town brains on the harbor.

taxi.fareNote: Cabs are metered; Uber and Lyft are widely used and often cheaper than street taxis.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Tourist areas are safe, but parts of Roxbury, Dorchester and Mattapan away from main corridors see gang-related violence at night.
Skip the 'Mass and Cass' (Massachusetts Ave/Melnea Cass) area with its open drug scene, and avoid lingering in Boston Common or downtown parks late at night.

hood_desc: Elegant Victorian brownstones, the boutiques and cafes of Newbury Street, and grand Commonwealth Avenue; a central, upscale base for shopping, dining, and easy access to the whole city.

One of America's oldest neighborhoods, all gas lamps, brick sidewalks, and cobblestoned Acorn Street, climbing up to the golden-domed Massachusetts State House; postcard-perfect for sightseeing and history.
Boston's Little Italy: narrow streets packed with red-sauce trattorias, cannoli bakeries, and wine bars, plus Freedom Trail sights like the Old North Church; the go-to for dining and evenings out.
The compact, walkable core wrapping Boston Common and the Financial District, where the Freedom Trail begins; the most convenient first-timer base with T lines converging and sights on your doorstep.
Across the Charles River, home to Harvard and MIT: leafy Harvard Square with its bookshops, coffeehouses, live music, and student energy; brainy, indie, and endlessly browsable.
lodging: Copley Square Hotel, A Found Hotel
Club Quarters Hotel Faneuil Hall, Boston

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: The subway (the 'T') runs roughly 5:00 AM to about 1:00 AM; there is no all-night service, so ride apps or late buses cover the overnight gap.
transit.pay: Fares use the CharlieCard: tap a reusable CharlieCard, CharlieTicket, or cash at the gate. A subway ride is $2.40 and a local bus is $1.70, and a transfer between them is included. CharlieCards are free from fare vending machines in most stations. The MBTA is rolling out contactless tap-to-pay with bank cards and phones.

bus: South Station Bus Terminal (Greyhound, Peter Pan, FlixBus, Megabus)

Free Massport shuttle to Blue Line 'Airport' station, then subway downtown (~20-30 min)

tip.r: 18-20% at restaurants and bars is expected; $1-2 per bag for porters and a few dollars for taxis.

food.name: New England clam chowder
food.desc: Thick cream chowder of quahogs, potato and salt pork, served with oyster crackers. Never red, never thin, and best in a cup so you can eat more after.

places.name: Neptune Oyster
places.note: Tiny 42-seat counter widely called the city's gold standard; no reservations, expect a wait.

places.name: Union Oyster House
places.note: Open since 1826, America's oldest continuously operating restaurant; sit at the oyster bar.

places.name: Legal Sea Foods
places.note: The chowder that has been served at presidential inaugurations; dependable and everywhere.

food.name: Lobster roll
food.desc: Knuckle and claw meat in a griddled split-top bun, either cold with mayo or Connecticut-style hot with drawn butter. Boston does both well.

places.name: Neptune Oyster
places.note: The hot buttered roll here is the one people fly in for; order it with fries.

places.name: Eventide Fenway
places.note: Brown butter lobster roll on a steamed Chinese bao-style bun; fast and excellent.

places.name: James Hook and Co.
places.note: Fifth-generation lobster wholesaler selling overstuffed rolls from a harborside shack.

food.name: North Shore roast beef sandwich
food.desc: Rare roast beef shaved paper-thin, piled on an onion roll and dressed three-way: James River barbecue sauce, mayo and American cheese.

places.name: Kelly's Roast Beef
places.note: Invented the beachside roast beef sandwich in 1951; eat it on the seawall.

places.name: Nick's Roast Beef
places.note: Making them since 1975 and repeatedly voted the region's best three-way.

places.name: Atha's Deli
places.note: Local favorite praised for the beef-to-sauce ratio; sports memorabilia on the walls.

food.name: Cannoli
food.desc: Crisp fried shell piped to order with sweet ricotta, dipped in chocolate chips or pistachio. The North End's loudest and most enjoyable argument.

places.name: Mike's Pastry
places.note: The famous string-tied blue box; huge shells, dozens of fillings, cash-friendly line.

places.name: Modern Pastry
places.note: Locals' pick: smaller, filled to order, crunchier shell and less sweet ricotta.

places.name: Bova's Bakery
places.note: Open 24 hours since 1926, so it settles any 2am cannoli debate.

food.name: Boston cream pie
food.desc: Not a pie but a sponge cake split and filled with vanilla custard under a chocolate glaze. Invented at the Parker House hotel in 1856.

places.name: Omni Parker House
places.note: Where it was created; eat the original in the hotel's Last Hurrah bar or take a slice to go.

places.name: Flour Bakery and Cafe
places.note: Joanne Chang's version of the classic, alongside her famous sticky buns.

places.name: Bova's Bakery
places.note: Old-school Italian bakery slice, available around the clock.

food.name: New England oysters
food.desc: Island Creek, Wellfleet and Duxbury oysters shucked to order, cold and briny, with mignonette and a squeeze of lemon.

places.name: Select Oyster Bar
places.note: Small Newbury Street basement room with a tight, very fresh Massachusetts oyster list.

places.name: Row 34
places.note: Oyster-and-craft-beer pairing done properly, from the Island Creek Oysters team.

places.name: Little Whale Oyster Bar
places.note: Cozy Newbury Street nod to coastal New England clam shacks; good happy hour.

food.name: Dunkin' iced coffee
food.desc: Massachusetts-born Dunkin' is the region's default coffee, and Bostonians drink it iced in February without irony. Order it regular for cream and sugar.

places.name: Dunkin'
places.note: One of hundreds across Greater Boston; the local ritual more than a destination.

places.name: George Howell Coffee
places.note: If you want the serious version, Howell helped build American specialty coffee.

food.name: Boston craft beer
food.desc: New England IPAs, hazy and juicy, plus the Sam Adams lagers that helped start the American craft movement. Taprooms cluster near the waterfront.

places.name: Trillium Brewing Company
places.note: The city's most sought-after hazy IPAs; big taproom and a seasonal beer garden.

places.name: Samuel Adams Downtown Boston Taproom
places.note: Central spot for small-batch pours from Boston's best known brewery.

places.name: Night Shift Brewing
places.note: Harbor-view patio near TD Garden with Detroit-style pizza alongside the beer.

landmarks: Fenway Park
America's oldest baseball park (1912), with its famous Green Monster wall, is a beloved sports landmark.
Boston Public Library
The grand Renaissance Revival Central Library at Copley Square features an ornate courtyard and reading rooms.
Faneuil Hall & Quincy Market
This historic marketplace and 'Cradle of Liberty' meeting hall buzzes with street performers and colonial architecture.
Boston Public Garden
America's first public botanical garden features the iconic swan boats gliding across its lagoon.
Bunker Hill Monument
This granite obelisk in Charlestown commemorates the famous Revolutionary War battle and offers panoramic city views.
USS Constitution
'Old Ironsides,' the world's oldest commissioned warship afloat, sits picturesquely in Charlestown Navy Yard.
Massachusetts State House
Charles Bulfinch's gold-domed 1798 capitol building crowns Beacon Hill and gleams in the sunlight.
Trinity Church
H.H. Richardson's Romanesque masterpiece reflects strikingly in the glass facade of the neighboring Hancock Tower.
Long Wharf & Custom House Tower
The historic waterfront wharf and clock-topped Custom House Tower frame classic harbor and skyline shots.
Zakim Bridge
The illuminated cable-stayed Leonard P. Zakim Bunker Hill Bridge is a dramatic modern gateway to the city skyline.

train.note: No train crosses the border from New England - the old Montrealer was withdrawn decades ago, so Canada is a coach or plane trip. From South Station, Amtrak's Acela and Northeast Regional run frequently to Providence, New York and Washington, and the Lake Shore Limited leaves each afternoon for Chicago with sleepers. North Station is a separate terminal roughly a mile away and handles the Downeaster to Portland and Brunswick in Maine; there is no through rail link between the two, so allow time to cross the city. MBTA Commuter Rail fans out to Worcester, Providence, Lowell and Cape Cod-bound connections.

bus.note: Almost everything leaves from the South Station Bus Terminal stacked above the train station, which is about as central as it gets and is on the Red and Silver lines. Ten carriers use it, including Greyhound, FlixBus, Megabus, Peter Pan, Concord Coach Lines, C&J, Dartmouth Coach, DATTCO, Boston Express and Plymouth & Brockton. Greyhound's Montreal run takes roughly seven to eight hours and everybody gets off the coach for passport control at the Vermont-Quebec border, so pad your schedule. Tickets are sold online and at counters in the terminal.

intl.to: Provincetown, Cape Cod (USA) - departs 200 Seaport Blvd in the Seaport District
Hingham, Hull, Charlestown & the Boston Harbor Islands (USA) - departs Long Wharf and Rowes Wharf

ferry.note: The Provincetown fast ferry is the star: about 90 minutes across Massachusetts Bay from the Seaport District, versus three hours or more by road around the Cape, and it runs daily in the warm months rather than year round. MBTA harbour boats from Long Wharf and Rowes Wharf to Hingham, Hull and Charlestown do run all year and take bikes. No international ferry sails from Boston - the CAT to Yarmouth, Nova Scotia, leaves from Bar Harbor, Maine, roughly five hours north by road, and only in summer. Book summer Provincetown sailings ahead; foot passengers only on the fast ferries.

half.name: Salem
half.blurb: Coastal town famous for the 1692 witch trials, with museums, historic courthouses and a walkable colonial waterfront.

half.name: Concord and Lexington
half.blurb: Revolutionary War battle sites where the first shots of the war were fired, preserved as national historical parks.

half.name: Plymouth
half.blurb: Site of the Pilgrims' 1620 landing, with Plymouth Rock, a replica Mayflower ship and a living-history colonial village.

full.name: Cape Cod (Provincetown)
full.blurb: Sandy peninsula of beach towns and dunes, with Provincetown's whale-watching boats and historic art colony at its tip.

full.name: Newport
full.blurb: Gilded Age resort town lined with Vanderbilt-era mansions along the Cliff Walk overlooking Narragansett Bay.
